statement: Partition-key ordering has one complete hostile-input-safe owner: supported values are validated before equality; SQLite-BINARY-compatible UTF-8 ordering and numeric/TEXT routing are preserved; unsupported/non-finite/boxed/exotic same-reference values fail closed before coercion; split metadata and target IDs are consumed from own data properties without accessors, inheritance, or iterator semantics; mutable JavaScript intrinsics cannot change comparison or split-target routing; merge table IDs are primitive-string-only and never coerced through mutable String; and KeyRange, PartitionResolver, QueryGroup plus split/merge sort and adjacency use the actual owned comparator expressions.

constraints.statement: Supersedes partition-key-ordering-owner-completion-v3 after category-complete Copilot PR #84 found two residual defects not measured by the sealed v3 predicate: pre-validation same-reference equality admitted unsupported/non-finite values, and the captured Array.isArray witness never engaged split-target resolution while destructuring still consumed Array iteration. Preserve v3's sealed predicate and evidence unchanged.

Absent bounds and supported equal number/string/Buffer keys may compare equal only through their typed paths. Unsupported, boxed, exotic, boolean, Symbol and non-finite numeric values must not bypass validation merely because both operands are identical.

Split-target resolution uses the module-captured Array.isArray result and indexed access to targetPartitionIds; it must remain correct after Array.isArray and Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator] are replaced, with no destructuring/iterator dependency.
Primitive string keys use deterministic SQLite BINARY-compatible UTF-8 byte order, including BMP/non-BMP cases that differ from JavaScript UTF-16 relational order.

Only finite number, primitive string, Buffer, absent bounds and the explicit numeric-vs-text-encoded-number compatibility case are comparable. Unsupported values fail closed with the exact typed split-key mismatch before user-controlled coercion.

Partition-key comparison and split-target routing capture every mutable intrinsic they need at module load. Replacing Buffer, Number, String, RegExp.test, Error, Array.isArray or Array iteration after import must not alter valid outcomes.
The doneWhen predicate and behavioral witnesses prove the actual split/merge sort and adjacency expressions call compareRoutingKeys; unrelated/dead tokens cannot satisfy closure.

Preserve numeric-key-routing: finite number/number stays numeric and a number against a text-encoded numeric persisted boundary compares numerically. Persisted large-integer representation remains A2.
Persisted type metadata, exact large-integer representation, encoding migration and old-boundary revalidation remain A2.
No Raft runtime, consensus transport, lifecycle, membership or formation behavior changes.
SQLite/non-BMP order, exact mismatch, same-reference refusal, mutable-intrinsic split-target routing and merge adjacency each need right-reason red controls where isolated controls are available.
Any src/ candidate needs category-complete independent verification newer than the last v4 attempt covering both sealed verificationTemplates with evidence paths.
Every equal numeric comparison returns canonical +0, including -0 versus 0, through both compareRoutingKeys and compareSplitKey; JavaScript -0 is not a distinct comparator result.

resolveSplitTargetPartitionId consumes splitKey and targetPartitionIds only from own data properties, does not invoke accessors, does not accept inherited routing metadata, validates the real Array without iterator/destructuring semantics, and captures its descriptor/own-property intrinsics at module load.

Merge sorting accepts only absent or primitive-string table IDs, validates non-absent types before equality, never consults mutable global String, and never invokes user-controlled coercion for table identity.

Each mutable intrinsic or metadata seam has an isolated witness where feasible, so one early failure cannot mask Buffer, Number, RegExp, Error, Array, Object-descriptor, iterator, or manager-String regressions.
